So what happens is they're losing their minds. This is a self-portrait of an artist who documented himself losing his mind. When he was first diagnosed, he drew a picture of himself. A year later, he drew another picture, and so on. By this time, he's completely lost his sense of being.

The artist is shedding his artifice. He’s shedding his clothing and revealing his true self. Alzheimer's involves losing your socialization because you're losing your ability to speak, verbalize ideas, and communicate with others. Three things remain: spiritual desires, singing, and drawing. Many people with Alzheimer's suddenly become religious or start going to church, singing, and painting despite never having done so before.

During the ice age era, we all believed in coexisting with ghosts, spirits, and fairies. Even though medically speaking, these people hear voices that aren't there, the reason is they always existed; we just forgot about them because of socialization.

An artist using psychedelics draws a cat as a divine entity, seeing its energy field, memory, aspirations, and intuition. This shows how time and space are irrelevant in such experiences, making art incomprehensible yet vibrant. Ventang Go, the greatest painter ever, sheds his socialization to create vivid, unique works like Star Night and Sunflower.

Summarizing, we've been brainwashed into believing humans are driven by material desires, but this isn't true.
